panels.title: 📊 Span Queue Size
panels.description: One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: 🚨 Span Queue Rejections
panels.description: One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: ⚡ Bulk Loader Insertion Time
panels.description: One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: 💓 Bulk Loader Aliveness
panels.description: One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: 📊 Bulk Loader Insertion Time Percentiles
panels.description: One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: ⚡ Bulk Loader Average Insertion Time
panels.description: One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: 🗑️ Dropped Spans (per min)
panels.description: Accepted spans released without being saved. span_error: individual spans failed to insert. transaction_error: the batch transaction failed. retry_exhausted: the batch kept hitting deadlocks or serialization failures. unresolved commit: the outcome of the commit is unknown, so the spans may be missing or saved without notifications. One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: ⏱️ Time Since Last Span Insert
panels.description: Seconds since a transaction last inserted spans. Unlike Bulk Loader Aliveness, this keeps rising while every insert fails. It also rises when no traces arrive. One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: 💥 Bulk Loader Exceptions (per min)
panels.description: Exceptions while inserting individual spans, and exceptions in the bulk loader loop itself. One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: 🧾 Evaluations Inserted (per min)
panels.description: Evaluations the bulk loader inserted per minute. One line per Phoenix replica: each replica has its own span queue and bulk loader.

panels.title: 📨 OTLP Trace Requests (per min)
panels.description: OTLP/HTTP export requests received at /v1/traces. Each request can carry many spans. gRPC exports are not included.

panels.title: ⌛ OTLP Request Latency (avg)
panels.description: Average time to accept an OTLP/HTTP export request. Spans are queued for insertion, so this does not include database time.

panels.title: 🚨 OTLP Request Exceptions (per min)
panels.description: Unhandled exceptions raised while handling /v1/traces requests, by exception type.

panels.title: 💾 Database Disk Usage
panels.description: Database disk usage as a share of allocated capacity, and whether span insertion is blocked. Reported only when PHOENIX_DATABASE_ALLOCATED_STORAGE_CAPACITY_GIBIBYTES and a usage threshold are set; the devops stack sets neither.

panels.title: 🧠 Container Memory vs Limit
panels.description: Working-set memory as a share of each container's memory limit. The kernel kills a container that reaches its limit. Python processes often keep freed memory, so usage can stay high after a load spike.

panels.title: 🧪 Datagen Throughput (per min)
panels.description: Traces per minute datagen is set to send, and how many the collector accepted or rejected. Delivered below the configured rate with failures above zero means Phoenix is shedding load; see Span Queue Rejections. Empty unless the datagen profile is running.

panels.title: 🚦 Datagen Export Failure Ratio
panels.description: Share of datagen's trace exports that failed over the last 5 minutes. Datagen does not retry, so failed traces never arrive.

panels.title: ⏸️ Datagen State
panels.description: 1 while replay is paused or datasets are still seeding, and the configured burstiness (0 is uniform). Change these at http://localhost:18273/datagen/.

targets.expr: sum(max by (evaluation_target) (phoenix_online_eval_pending_work_units)) + sum(max by (evaluation_target) (phoenix_online_eval_running_work_units)) + sum(max by (evaluation_target) (phoenix_online_eval_retryable_error_work_units))

panels.title: 🧮 Online Eval Queue Size
panels.description: Online evaluations queued across span, trace, and session work: pending, running, and awaiting a retry. The queue has no size limit, so overload shows as growth here. Each count stops at a fixed bound per target and status.

panels.title: 🎛️ Online Eval Evaluator Slots In Use
panels.description: Running work units across all targets divided by the evaluator concurrency limit (PHOENIX_ONLINE_EVAL_MAX_EVALUATOR_CONCURRENCY), which span, trace, and session work share.

panels.title: 🧪 Online Eval Evaluator Duration
panels.description: Seconds inside the evaluator call, including sandbox queueing and calls cut off at the execution deadline, for all targets. Quantiles are interpolated within histogram buckets (for example 5 to 10 s), so the average is the better guide when calls take a fixed time.

panels.title: 📞 Online Eval Evaluator Calls (per min)
panels.description: Evaluator calls per minute across all targets, by evaluator kind. Summed across replicas.

panels.title: 🧮 Span Eval Queue
panels.description: Span work units in the queue now, by status. Retryable errors are waiting out a cooldown before another attempt. Every replica reports the same value, so this takes the max.

panels.title: 🪦 Span Eval Terminal Work (window)
panels.description: Span work units that ended as failed (out of retries), expired, or cleared, and were last updated within the terminal-metrics window. Every replica reports the same value, so this takes the max.

panels.title: ⏳ Span Eval Oldest Pending Age
panels.description: How long the oldest pending span work unit has waited to start. 0 when nothing is pending. A steady climb means evaluations are not keeping up.

panels.title: 📈 Span Eval Throughput (per min)
panels.description: Span work units queued, and work units that left the queue by outcome, per minute. Queued above evaluated means the backlog is growing. Summed across replicas.

panels.title: ⏱️ Span Eval Queue-to-Result Lag
panels.description: Seconds from queueing a span evaluation to its successful result; the lag the evaluators pages show. Quantiles are interpolated within histogram buckets (for example 120 to 300 s), so read them as ranges. It leaves out the span producer's wait before queueing; see Span Producer Lag & Ingest Rate.

panels.title: 🌊 Span Producer Lag & Ingest Rate
panels.description: Span cursor lag (left axis): roughly how far, in seconds of ingest, the span producer trails the newest span, computed as the distance in span ids from the cursor to the newest span divided by the ingest rate. The producer waits 60 seconds before scanning newly observed spans, so 60 to 140 seconds is normal. It jumps while the ingest rate changes quickly and shows no data while nothing is ingested. Ingest rate (right axis): growth of the highest span id between producer ticks, which is the rate spans are stored, across all projects.

panels.title: 🧮 Trace Eval Queue
panels.description: Trace work units in the queue now, by status. Retryable errors are waiting out a cooldown before another attempt. Every replica reports the same value, so this takes the max.

panels.title: 🪦 Trace Eval Terminal Work (window)
panels.description: Trace work units that ended as failed (out of retries), expired, or cleared, and were last updated within the terminal-metrics window. Every replica reports the same value, so this takes the max.

panels.title: ⏳ Trace Eval Oldest Pending Age
panels.description: How long the oldest pending trace work unit has waited to start. 0 when nothing is pending. A steady climb means evaluations are not keeping up.

panels.title: 📈 Trace Eval Throughput (per min)
panels.description: Trace work units queued, and work units that left the queue by outcome, per minute. Queued above evaluated means the backlog is growing. Summed across replicas.

panels.title: ⏱️ Trace Eval Queue-to-Result Lag
panels.description: Seconds from queueing a trace evaluation to its successful result; the lag the evaluators pages show. Quantiles are interpolated within histogram buckets (for example 120 to 300 s), so read them as ranges. It starts after the evaluation delay, which the sweeper waits out before queueing.

panels.title: 🔁 Trace Sweeps (per min)
panels.description: Committed and failed or rolled-back trace sweeps per minute. Each sweep looks for traces whose evaluation delay has passed.

panels.title: 🐢 Trace Sweep Duration
panels.description: Trace sweep duration percentiles.

panels.title: 📥 Trace Sweep Eligible Evaluations
panels.description: Trace evaluations on the latest sweep page that pass their evaluator's filter. A page holds at most 1,000.

panels.title: 🌊 Trace Decided-Through Lag
panels.description: Largest time by which a trace's latest span postdates the activity its completed evaluation covered, over the terminal-metrics window. A large value means spans keep arriving after the evaluation delay, so the delay may be shorter than the quiet gaps in that traffic.
